text_blocks.snippet: It is recommended to get vaccinated against COVID-19 even if you have previously been infected with the virus. Here are some key points to consider:
snippet_highlighted_words: It is recommended to get vaccinated against COVID-19 even if you have previously been infected with the virus

list.snippet: Natural immunity from a previous infection may wane over time.
Vaccination can provide additional and broader protection against different variants of the virus.
It is generally recommended to wait 3 months after recovering from a COVID-19 infection before getting vaccinated.
This allows your body to fully develop its natural immunity before receiving the vaccine.
Vaccination can help prevent reinfection, especially with emerging variants.
It can also reduce the severity of symptoms if you do get infected again.
Vaccination contributes to herd immunity and protects vulnerable populations.
It is important to consult with your healthcare provider to discuss your individual vaccination plan.
They can assess your medical history and determine the best vaccination schedule for you.
If you have a severe or prolonged case of COVID-19, it is advisable to delay vaccination until you have fully recovered.
You can still get vaccinated even if you have mild symptoms of COVID-19, as long as you are not actively infectious.

text_blocks.snippet: Remember, vaccination remains one of the most effective ways to protect yourself and others from COVID-19.
